title: Without Vendor Order Management View, Returns cannot be opened
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that can open Parts → Returns.
  • {User-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL NORETVIEW) is a staff member at {Location-A} whose custom role {Role-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL NORETVIEW) has 'Part Library & Inventory → View' and no 'Vendor Order Management' permission.
  • {User-B} is signed in at {Location-A} in a second browser or a private window.
custom_steps:
1. As the Admin, go to Parts → Returns.
  2. As {User-B}, go to Parts → Inventory.
  3. Look for Returns in the Parts side menu.
  4. If Returns is offered, click it.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: The Returns list opens for the Admin.
  • Step 2: The Inventory list opens for {User-B}, so the Parts section is open to this user.
  • Steps 3 and 4: {User-B} cannot open Parts → Returns: either Returns is not offered in the Parts side menu, or clicking it does not open the Returns list. Write in the result comment which one you saw.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S9-N3a, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas 13 Oct copy: no board shows a role without Vendor Order Management; every Parts board shows "Returns" under "SUPPLY CHAIN" in the side menu. Product's answer of 13 Oct (Chris Ward, question 10). SV-10822 does not yet carry S9-N3a (the PRD wins). Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-N3a: “Opening Parts → Returns needs 'Vendor Order Management → View'. Starting a vendor return needs 'Vendor Order Management → Create & Edit'. A role with both and without 'Part Library & Inventory → View' opens a return and gets the S9-N3 access error when it searches for a part.”
